PLAINTIFF'S MOTION TO COMPEL ANSWERS TO INTERROGATORIES AND PRODUCTION OF DOCUMENTS

Plaintiff Larkspur Timber Supply LLC, by its attorneys, moves under Illinois Supreme Court Rules 213(d) and 214 and Rule 219(a) for an order compelling Defendant Northgate Millwork Company to answer Interrogatories 4, 7, 9, and 12 and to produce documents responsive to Requests 3, 5, and 8, and for the reasonable expenses incurred in bringing this motion. In support, Plaintiff states as follows.

INTRODUCTION

This is a straightforward collection case. Plaintiff delivered 184,000 board feet of kiln-dried white oak under a purchase order; Defendant accepted every lot, paid three invoices, and has not paid the last three. Defendant's answer asserts that the goods were nonconforming. Plaintiff served interrogatories and document requests directed at exactly that defense. Defendant answered seven of twelve interrogatories, objected to the rest as "overly broad and unduly burdensome" without explanation, and produced 214 pages, none of which concerns the alleged nonconformity. The Court should grant this motion and compel complete answers.

FACTUAL AND PROCEDURAL BACKGROUND

1. Plaintiff filed this action on March 30, 2026. Defendant answered on May 4, 2026, asserting as its second affirmative defense that the goods delivered under lots four through six were nonconforming.

2. On May 18, 2026, Plaintiff served its First Set of Interrogatories and First Request for Production. True and correct copies are attached to the Declaration of Dashiell Tsukamoto as Exhibits A and B.

3. Defendant served responses on June 24, 2026, after a 14-day extension Plaintiff granted. Copies are attached as Exhibits C and D.

4. Interrogatories 4, 7, 9, and 12 ask Defendant to identify the lots alleged to be nonconforming, the respect in which each was nonconforming, the persons who inspected them, and the date and manner of any notice of nonconformity given to Plaintiff. Defendant objected to each as "overly broad and unduly burdensome" and answered none.

5. Requests 3, 5, and 8 seek Defendant's inspection records, internal communications concerning the lots, and any communication to Plaintiff asserting nonconformity. Defendant produced no document in response to any of the three.

6. Counsel for Plaintiff wrote to counsel for Defendant on July 1 and July 22, 2026, identifying each deficiency and requesting a conference. Counsel conferred by telephone on August 5, 2026. Defendant agreed to supplement by August 19, 2026 and has not done so. The parties have complied with Illinois Supreme Court Rule 201(k), and further attempts at resolution would be futile.

ARGUMENT

I. THE INFORMATION SOUGHT IS PLAINLY RELEVANT TO DEFENDANT'S OWN AFFIRMATIVE DEFENSE.

A party may obtain discovery of any matter relevant to the subject matter of the pending action. Ill. S. Ct. R. 201(b)(1). Relevance at the discovery stage is broader than at trial and includes matter reasonably calculated to lead to admissible evidence. Interrogatories 4, 7, 9, and 12 ask which lots were nonconforming, how, who says so, and when Defendant told Plaintiff. Defendant pleaded that defense; it cannot now decline to describe it.

II. A BOILERPLATE OBJECTION IS NOT AN OBJECTION.

An objection must state the specific ground on which it rests. A general recitation that a request is "overly broad and unduly burdensome," unaccompanied by any explanation of the burden or any attempt to answer to the extent the request is proper, is insufficient and waives the objection. Defendant has not described the volume of material it would have to review, the effort involved, or any respect in which the requests exceed the scope of Rule 201(b)(1). Defendant did not seek a protective order.

III. THE PRODUCTION IS FACIALLY INCOMPLETE.

Defendant asserts that it inspected the goods and found them nonconforming, yet produced no inspection record and no internal communication about any lot. Either the documents exist and were withheld, or the defense has no documentary support. In either case Defendant must answer: if documents are withheld on privilege, Rule 201(n) requires a privilege log, and none was served.

IV. EXPENSES ARE WARRANTED UNDER RULE 219(a).

Rule 219(a) provides that if a party fails to comply with discovery, the court shall require the offending party to pay the reasonable expenses, including attorney fees, incurred in obtaining the order, unless the court finds the failure was substantially justified. Defendant's failure was not justified: it agreed to supplement and simply did not. Plaintiff seeks $3,850, supported by the fee declaration attached as Exhibit E.

CONCLUSION

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff Larkspur Timber Supply LLC respectfully requests that the Court enter an order (a) compelling Defendant to answer Interrogatories 4, 7, 9, and 12 in full within fourteen (14) days; (b) compelling Defendant to produce all documents responsive to Requests 3, 5, and 8 within fourteen (14) days, or to serve a privilege log identifying any document withheld; (c) awarding Plaintiff its reasonable expenses of $3,850 under Rule 219(a); and (d) granting such other relief as the Court deems just. A proposed order is submitted with this motion.
